# The check catalogue

Every check the kit runs against a server, with the sentence of the specification it
enforces. Severity follows the keyword in that sentence — MUST is an error, SHOULD a
warning, anything else a note — and the few checks that are stricter than their keyword
say why. `tests/unit/test_spec_quotes.py` verifies every quote against the specification
text, and `tests/unit/test_checks_fire.py` proves every check fails against a server that
breaks its rule.

## Layer 1 — Protocol and transport

### H-001 · A foreign Origin is rejected with 403

**error** · handshake + stateless · http

> Servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks. If the Origin header is present and invalid, servers MUST respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/transports/streamable-http](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#security--endpoint)

### H-002 · A notification is acknowledged with 202 and no body

**error** · handshake + stateless · http

> If the server accepts it, the server MUST return HTTP status code 202 Accepted with no body.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/transports/streamable-http](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#sending-messages)

### H-003 · Responses use a content type the client must support

**error** · handshake + stateless · http

> the server MUST return either Content-Type: application/json (a single JSON object) or Content-Type: text/event-stream (an SSE response stream).
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/transports/streamable-http](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#sending-messages)

### H-004 · Mcp-Method must agree with the body

**error** · stateless · http

> Servers that process the request body MUST reject requests where the values specified in the headers do not match the corresponding values in the request body. [...] servers MUST return HTTP status 400 Bad Request and MUST include a JSON-RPC error response using the following error code
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/transports/streamable-http](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#server-validation)

### H-005 · tools/call must carry Mcp-Name

**error** · stateless · http

> These headers are REQUIRED for compliance.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/transports/streamable-http](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#standard-request-headers)

### H-006 · MCP-Protocol-Version must agree with the envelope

**error** · stateless · http

> The header value MUST match the io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion field carried in the request body's _meta. If the values do not match, the server MUST reject the request with 400 Bad Request and a HeaderMismatch JSON-RPC error
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/transports/streamable-http](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#protocol-version-header)

### H-007 · An unknown method returns HTTP 404

**error** · stateless · http

> If the server does not implement the requested RPC method, it MUST respond with 404 Not Found and a JSON-RPC error with code -32601 (Method not found).
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/transports/streamable-http](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#protocol-version-header)

### H-008 · A missing or invalid token is refused with 401

**error** · handshake + stateless · http · needs: auth

> Invalid or expired tokens MUST receive a HTTP 401 response.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/authorization](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization#token-handling)

### H-009 · A client can find out where to get a token

**error** · handshake + stateless · http · needs: auth

> MCP servers MUST implement one of the following discovery mechanisms to provide authorization server location information to MCP clients
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/authorization/authorization-server-discovery](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/authorization-server-discovery#protected-resource-metadata-discovery-requirements)

### H-010 · A token issued for someone else is refused

**error** · handshake + stateless · http · needs: auth, foreign_tokens

> MCP servers MUST only accept tokens specifically intended for themselves and MUST reject tokens that do not include them in the audience claim or otherwise verify that they are the intended recipient of the token.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/authorization/security-considerations](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations#access-token-privilege-restriction)

### P-001 · Responses echo the request id

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> Result responses MUST include the same ID as the request they correspond to.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#result-responses)

### P-002 · Results match the specification's schema

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> This specification defines the authoritative protocol requirements, based on the TypeScript schema in schema.ts.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · overview](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28)

*Stricter than its keyword because:* The schema is the specification's own definition of every message; a result that fails it is malformed by the specification's definition, whatever keyword the prose around it uses.

### P-003 · An unknown method is answered with -32601

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> If the server does not implement the requested RPC method, it MUST respond with 404 Not Found and a JSON-RPC error with code -32601 (Method not found).
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/transports/streamable-http](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#protocol-version-header)

### P-004 · Tool names follow the naming rules

**warning** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> Tool names SHOULD be between 1 and 128 characters in length (inclusive). [...] The following SHOULD be the only allowed characters: uppercase and lowercase ASCII letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), underscore (_), hyphen (-), and dot (.)
>
> — [2026-07-28 · server/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#tool-names)

### P-005 · Every inputSchema is a valid JSON Schema object

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> inputSchema: JSON Schema defining expected parameters [...] MUST be a valid JSON Schema object (not null)
>
> — [2026-07-28 · server/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#tool)

### P-006 · Every outputSchema is a valid JSON Schema

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> Schemas MUST be valid according to their declared or default dialect
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#schema-validation)

### P-007 · tools/list is returned in a stable order

**warning** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> Servers SHOULD return tools in a deterministic order (i.e., the same ordering across requests when the underlying set of tools has not changed).
>
> — [2026-07-28 · server/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#listing-tools)

### P-008 · The tool set does not vary per connection

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> This set MAY be empty and MAY change over time [...] but MUST NOT vary per-connection or as a side effect of other requests on the connection.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · server/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#listing-tools)

### P-009 · Results identify the server in _meta

**warning** · stateless · stdio + http

> Servers SHOULD include the following io.modelcontextprotocol/* field in every result's _meta, unless specifically configured not to do so, to identify themselves without relying on any prior connection state
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#_meta)

### P-010 · server/discover is implemented

**error** · stateless · stdio + http

> server/discover lets a client query a server's supported protocol versions, capabilities, and identity before sending any other requests. Servers MUST implement it.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · server/discover](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover)

### P-011 · An unsupported protocol version is refused with -32022

**error** · stateless · stdio + http

> If the server does not implement the requested protocol version [...] it MUST respond with 400 Bad Request and an UnsupportedProtocolVersionError listing its supported versions.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/transports/streamable-http](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#protocol-version-header)

### P-012 · A request without the per-request envelope is refused with -32602

**error** · stateless · stdio + http

> A request missing any required field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code -32602 (Invalid params). On HTTP, the response status MUST be 400 Bad Request.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#_meta)

### P-013 · initialize negotiates a version the server supports

**error** · handshake · stdio + http

> If the server supports the requested protocol version, it MUST respond with the same version. Otherwise, the server MUST respond with another protocol version it supports.
>
> — [2025-11-25 · basic/lifecycle](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#version-negotiation)

### P-014 · stdout carries nothing but MCP messages

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio

> The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/transports/stdio](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio)

### P-015 · The server exits when stdin is closed

**warning** · handshake + stateless · stdio

> Servers SHOULD exit promptly when their standard input is closed or reads return end-of-file.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic/transports/stdio](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio#shutdown)

### P-016 · A malformed message does not take the server down

**warning** · handshake + stateless · stdio

> MCP uses the standard JSON-RPC 2.0 error codes (-32700, -32600 to -32603) for general protocol failures.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#error-codes)

*Stricter than its keyword because:* The specification defines the parse error but not what happens after it; a server that exits on one malformed line takes every in-flight request on the connection with it.

### P-017 · Requests in flight together are answered correctly

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio

> Result responses MUST include the same ID as the request they correspond to.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · basic](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#result-responses)

### P-018 · A slow call does not block the connection

**warning** · handshake + stateless · stdio

No normative sentence: engineering practice ([context](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic)).

*Stricter than its keyword because:* Nothing in the specification forbids handling one request at a time. In practice a connection that stalls behind its slowest call makes every client sharing it hang, and it is almost always a blocking call left in async code.

### P-019 · The tools capability is declared

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> Servers that support tools MUST declare the tools capability
>
> — [2026-07-28 · server/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#capabilities)

### P-020 · An unknown tool is reported as a protocol error

**info** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> Protocol Errors indicate issues with the request structure itself that models are less likely to be able to fix: [...] They are returned as standard JSON-RPC errors
>
> — [2026-07-28 · server/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#error-handling)

## Layer 2 — Tool contracts and annotations

### A-001 · Read-only tools do not change anything

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http · needs: oracle, samples

> If true, the tool does not modify its environment.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · schema](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/schema#toolannotations)

*Stricter than its keyword because:* The specification calls annotations hints and tells clients not to trust them from untrusted servers. Clients still decide from them whether to ask the user before a call runs, so a false one removes that question; the kit treats it as a defect rather than a matter of style.

### A-002 · Tools that destroy things say so

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http · needs: oracle, samples, mutations

> If true, the tool may perform destructive updates to its environment. If false, the tool performs only additive updates.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · schema](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/schema#toolannotations)

*Stricter than its keyword because:* The specification calls annotations hints and tells clients not to trust them from untrusted servers. Clients still decide from them whether to ask the user before a call runs, so a false one removes that question; the kit treats it as a defect rather than a matter of style.

### A-003 · Idempotent tools really are

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http · needs: oracle, samples, mutations

> If true, calling the tool repeatedly with the same arguments will have no additional effect on its environment.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · schema](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/schema#toolannotations)

*Stricter than its keyword because:* The specification calls annotations hints and tells clients not to trust them from untrusted servers. Clients still decide from them whether to ask the user before a call runs, so a false one removes that question; the kit treats it as a defect rather than a matter of style.

### A-004 · Tools that change things carry annotations at all

**info** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http · needs: oracle, samples, mutations

> annotations: Optional properties describing tool behavior
>
> — [2026-07-28 · server/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#tool)

### C-001 · Arguments the schema allows are accepted

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> inputSchema: JSON Schema defining expected parameters
>
> — [2026-07-28 · server/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#tool)

*Stricter than its keyword because:* A published schema is the only contract a client has. Rejecting input the schema allows breaks every client that relied on it, and the client cannot tell from the schema that it will happen.

### C-002 · Arguments the schema forbids are refused, not crashed on

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> Servers MUST: Validate all tool inputs
>
> — [2026-07-28 · server/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#security-considerations)

### C-003 · structuredContent matches the published outputSchema

**error** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> If an output schema is provided: Servers MUST provide structured results that conform to this schema.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · server/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#output-schema)

### C-004 · Structured results also come back as text

**warning** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> For backwards compatibility, a tool that returns structured content SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block.
>
> — [2026-07-28 · server/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#structured-content)

### C-005 · Failed calls say something a model can act on

**warning** · handshake + stateless · stdio + http

> Tool Execution Errors contain actionable feedback that language models can use to self-correct and retry with adjusted parameters
>
> — [2026-07-28 · server/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#error-handling)

*Stricter than its keyword because:* An error result with no text gives the model nothing to correct, so it guesses or gives up.

## Layers 3 and 4

Authorization, tenancy, credential handling and upstream behaviour depend on the connector's
domain, so they are scenario tests rather than portable checks: see `tests/layer3_auth/` and
`tests/layer4_upstream/`. The portable parts — HTTP authorization (H-008 to H-010) and the
credential leak scan in `mcpqa.leaks` — are available to any suite.
